assertions: Asset has both Data Streams and Data Feed sources configured
A fresh Data Streams price P_new at timestamp T_new is already stored in s_dataStreamsPrice[asset]
An older but still-non-stale Streams report at T_old < T_new exists (e.g., a reorg / replay or workflow re-run)
setup_calls: priceAdmin transmits the report at T_new (price=P_new) — auction prices will use P_new
priceAdmin then transmits the report at T_old (price=P_old, P_old != P_new)

attack_steps: Asset has Data Streams feed configured with stalenessThreshold = S.
Workflow forwards a fresh report (timestamp T_new, price P_new) to WorkflowRouter.onReport, which routes to PriceManager.transmit. State now: s_dataStreamsPrice[asset] = {P_new, T_new}.
A subsequent on-chain Streams transmission (or a workflow re-run that reuses an earlier signed report still within stalenessThreshold) carries timestamp T_old < T_new and price P_old.

PriceManager.transmit verifies the report through verifierProxy.verifyBulk (signature-valid) and runs `if (report.observationsTimestamp < block.timestamp - feedInfo.stalenessThreshold) revert StaleFeedData();`.
Because T_old is still within stalenessThreshold (T_old >= block.timestamp - S), the staleness guard PASSES.
Code path L178-L179 unconditionally writes s_dataStreamsPrice[asset] = {P_old, T_old}, OVERWRITING the fresher entry.
All subsequent _getAssetPrice() calls (used by checkUpkeep, performUpkeep, bid, isValidSignature, getAssetOutAmount) now return the older P_old until a newer report is transmitted.

Bidder front-runs by triggering a forwarder call that delivers a stale-but-fresh-enough report just before submitting their bid, biasing the auction curve in their favor (e.g., when underlying price has moved up, bidder restores P_old < P_market and pays less assetOut for the same assetIn amount).
Inverse direction: a malicious or buggy workflow execution causes price regression that affects all live auctions and CowSwap orders signed via isValidSignature.
preconditions: Forwarder / PRICE_ADMIN_ROLE delivers reports in non-monotonic order (network reordering, retried workflow, multi-DON consolidation, or operator error).
Underlying market price moved between T_old and T_new such that P_old != P_new is exploitable.

triage.drop_reason: Hypothesis written but full Foundry PoC against the GPV2CompatibleAuction stack (requires deploying FeeAggregator + WorkflowRouter + AuctionBidder + 4 mocks + role grants) was deferred due to remaining budget. Code evidence: PriceManager.sol L162 only enforces lower-bound staleness — there is no `if (report.observationsTimestamp <= s_dataStreamsPrice[asset].timestamp) continue;` guard. The store at L178 is unconditional. By contrast _getAssetPrice() (L385-L401) at least picks the more-recent timestamp between Streams and DataFeed, demonstrating the developers were aware of monotonicity for read-side fallback but missed it on the write side. C4 Areas-of-Concern explicitly highlights 'auction curve' invariant and price-feed manipulation. PRICE_ADMIN_ROLE is held by WorkflowRouter (per README trusted-roles), so the trust boundary is the FORWARDER_ROLE, which routes Chainlink CRE workflow payloads — out-of-order delivery is realistic for chained workflows.

deployments: deploy:MockVerifierProxy that returns reports verbatim (signature already validated by Streams DON)

assertions: A signed Streams report exists with observationsTimestamp = T + 3600 (future)

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: ( s_dataStreamsPrice[asset].timestamp > block.timestamp ) && ( _getAssetPrice(asset, true) does not revert StaleFeedData even after S seconds elapse )

attack_steps: PriceManager.transmit L162 checks: `if (report.observationsTimestamp < block.timestamp - feedInfo.stalenessThreshold) revert StaleFeedData();`. There is NO upper bound check (e.g., `report.observationsTimestamp > block.timestamp + tolerance`).
A future-dated observationsTimestamp T_future > block.timestamp passes the lower-bound staleness check trivially (T_future >> T - S).
PriceManager stores s_dataStreamsPrice[asset] = {usdPrice, timestamp: T_future}.

_getAssetPrice (L378) computes minTimestamp = block.timestamp - stalenessThreshold. Branch at L385: `if (updatedAt < minTimestamp && usdDataFeed != 0)` — for the future-stamped entry, updatedAt = T_future >= minTimestamp, so the data-feed fallback is NEVER consulted as long as T_future > minTimestamp.
isStale check at L405: `bool isStale = updatedAt < minTimestamp;` — false. Price is treated as valid.

Effect: a single transmission with a future timestamp keeps the Streams price 'fresh' for (T_future - block.timestamp + stalenessThreshold) seconds, far beyond the intended stalenessThreshold window. During that window, any market move is invisible to the auction; bidders can exploit the stuck price.
Similarly relevant for `transmit` self-replay: report.expiresAt is also not validated against block.timestamp at L155 — an expired but still-fresh-by-observationsTimestamp report is accepted.
preconditions: DON or upstream report-generation pipeline emits a report whose observationsTimestamp drifts ahead of consumer chain block.timestamp (clock skew, cross-chain bridging, replay of previously-signed reports timestamped from a fork ahead in time, or operator-controlled offset).
PRICE_ADMIN_ROLE (held by WorkflowRouter; ultimately FORWARDER_ROLE-controlled CRE workflow payload) delivers the report.

triage.drop_reason: Code evidence is concrete (L162 lacks upper-bound check; L385 freshness branch hinges on `updatedAt < minTimestamp`). Severity hinges on whether a future-stamped Streams report can realistically be produced/replayed; depending on Chainlink Streams DON behavior this may be Low to Medium. Comparable issue patterns appear in Trace2Inv-T8 (oracle freshness invariants). PoC would require mocking VerifierProxy.verifyBulk to return a custom ReportV3 with a future observationsTimestamp and asserting that subsequent _getAssetPrice(asset, true) does not revert. Not built within remaining budget.

assertions: A workflowId W has been added with at least one target T
Admin then removes target T via applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates(W, [T], [])
setup_calls: admin: applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates([], [{W, [{T, [SEL]}]}])  // create W with one target
admin: applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates(W, [T], [])  // remove the only target

attack_steps: applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates removes-loop body (L143-L149):  `_applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates(workflowId, s_workflowInfos[workflowId].allowlistedTargets.values(), new TargetSelectors[](0));`
When allowlistedTargets is empty, this resolves to `_applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates(workflowId, [], [])`.
Inside _applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates (L184-L221), L192-L194: `if (removes.length == 0 && adds.length == 0) revert Errors.EmptyList();`
Therefore the entire applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates call reverts and the workflowId cannot be removed by this code path.

Workaround: admin must re-add a dummy target/selector to W and then call applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates again — extra transaction cost and operational burden, plus a window where W is allowlisted with a phantom target.
The same EmptyList revert blocks `applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates` even when the caller's intent is purely to remove an empty workflow, which is otherwise a legitimate cleanup operation.
preconditions: Admin previously emptied a workflow's targets via applyAllowlistedTargetsUpdates.

triage.drop_reason: Verified by source inspection (L143-149 + L192-194). Severity is Low (admin-only DoS with workaround) but the bug is concrete: the early EmptyList guard inside the helper does not account for being called as part of a workflowId removal where the helper's job is purely to clean up. Suggested fix: in the removes loop of applyAllowlistedWorkflowsUpdates, only call the helper when allowlistedTargets.length() > 0, or allow the helper to accept fully-empty input when invoked internally for cleanup. PoC would deploy WorkflowRouter, grant DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, run the four steps in setup_calls, and assertExpectRevert on the final call. Not built within remaining budget but trivially constructible.
